source_caption_text:
Never realised how crazy the bassline was on this 😭

When Gucci Mane released “Lemonade” in 2009, he took a simple idea and built an entire song around it. Produced by Bangladesh, the track appeared on The State vs. Radric Davis and stood out for its playful piano sample, heavy bass and children’s vocals on the hook. It quickly became one of Gucci’s most recognisable records.

The lyrics revolve around the colour yellow, with Gucci naming everything from yellow diamonds and cars to lemon pepper wings. His laid-back delivery makes the unusual theme feel effortless, while Bangladesh’s production gives the song a sound that’s instantly recognisable. The story behind it is just as memorable, with Gucci reportedly coming up with the yellow theme after mixing his drink with lemonade.

“Lemonade” went on to become a staple of 2000s hip-hop, inspiring countless freestyles and remixes over the years. Even now, the beat is easy to recognise from the opening piano notes, and Gucci’s approach to the track is a big reason it has remained so popular.
